newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Ross says Israel-PLO security links "set in motion".
newsitem.headline: Ross says Israel-PLO security links "set in motion".

text.p: Department comment)
By Paul Holmes
U.S. envoy Dennis Ross said on Tuesday Israel and the Palestinians had begun restoring security cooperation and their peacemaking would stand or fall on whether it brought results.
But Palestinians insisted political progress must accompany security ties and called on Israel to rescind stringent measures imposed after last month's twin suicide bombing in Jerusalem.

"This has been a good start and the process has been set in motion. We have to see the process produce results and we're working to that end," Ross told reporters after meeting Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in the West Bank town of Ramallah.
Arafat did not emerge from the meeting to speak to reporters.
In Washington, a State Department spokesman said Secretary of State Madeleine Albright was encouraged by the results of Ross's mission.

During their talks with Ross, the two sides determined a means of sharing information and acting together to combat "terrorism", spokesman James Rubin said, adding: "Now we're going to be looking for results, results, results."
Ross, who has brought Israeli, Palestinian and U.S. security experts together during his mission, said he expected to end his visit on Wednesday.

He flew to the region at the weekend after the attack at a Jerusalem market that killed 16 people including the two unidentified bombers threatened to shatter already fragile Israeli-Palestinian ties.

The difficulty of his task was driven home in the West Bank town of Nablus, where around 10,000 Palestinians marched in protest against U.S. and Israeli pressure on Arafat to crack down on the militants.
Witnesses said masked youths burned a dummy of Ross dressed as an ultra-Orthodox Jew holding a doll resembling Netanyahu.
"This is a message to Ross. Stop U.S. bias towards Israel and stop pressuring the Palestinian Authority to make concessions to Israel," one protester said.
Palestinian negotiator Nabil Shaath said Ross had extended his visit to Wednesday in order to convince Israel to lift the closure imposed on the West Bank and Gaza Strip and rescind other measures.

"I think Mr Ross is doing his best to get started and this means getting the tripartite security coordinations started and it also means for Israel to rescind all the measures it has taken against us," he told reporters in Ramallah.

Netanyahu, who flies to Jordan on Wednesday for talks with King Hussein on the crisis in the peace process, has accused Arafat of doing "damn all" to smash what he says is a "terrorist infrastructure" operating from Palestinian self-rule areas.
"The goal is not holding these (security) meetings but getting real results from these meetings. These things will be tested in the coming days, the coming weeks," he said.

He says real security cooperation from Arafat must come before any resumption of peace talks and before any significant lifting of sanctions he has slapped on Palestinian self-rule areas since the July 30 bombing.
Jordan said King Hussein, the first Arab leader to meet the Israeli leader since the attack, would urge Netanyahu to ease the sanctions at their summit in the Red Sea resort of Aqaba.
Israeli officials said Foreign Minister David Levy and National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon would join Netanyahu on the trip to Jordan.
Arafat has insisted he is making a "100 percent effort" on security and accuses Israel of using the bombing as a pretext to weaken his legitimacy.

The two bombers have not yet been identified nor has a claim of responsibility from the Moslem militant group Hamas been fully authenticated. Moslem militants have killed scores of Israelis in suicide attacks.
Israeli-Palestinian peace talks had already been in stalemate well before the bombing over a Jewish settlement Israel began building in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
Palestinians want construction halted, an end to Israel's demolition of Palestinian houses and land confiscations and a lifting of Netanyahu's punitive measures.

Albright, eager to bring the sides into accelerated final peace talks, is expected to make her first visit to the region late this month if she deems enough progress has been made on security cooperation.
